AccountProfileBody.description:
A self-service profile patch. EVERY field is optional — only provided
(non-None) fields are written; an omitted field is left unchanged. Clearing a
field is an explicit empty string / empty object (never null).
AccountProfileBody.title: AccountProfileBody

AnalyzeSampleRequest.description:
A pasted sample log/alert record for field-mapping suggestion (F9).

The ``sample`` is UNTRUSTED, attacker-influenceable log data (#9): it is flattened
to dotted paths and used ONLY to SUGGEST field mappings — never evaluated, never
persisted to the config doc. Only the operator-confirmed mapping NAMES are saved
later (via PUT /settings or POST /sources).
AnalyzeSampleRequest.title: AnalyzeSampleRequest

AppliesWhen.description:
When a runbook applies to a case. Every present criterion is any-of; all
present criteria must match. ``always`` marks only the Generic incident fallback
(the lowest specificity). Limits (checked by ``validate_runbook``): ``rule_ids``
at most 50 values of 1 to 256 characters; ``mitre`` at most 50 ``T####`` or
``T####.###`` ids (a parent matches its sub-techniques); ``sources`` at most 20
source ids or ``type:<SourceType>``; ``statuses`` at most 10 ``CaseStatus``
values; ``any_tags`` at most 20 tags of at most 64 characters.
AppliesWhen.title: AppliesWhen

AuditChange.description:
One changed field in a settings, user, role, rule or runbook write (SPEC
§4.5.3). A secret is written as ``{field, before: None, after: None, secret:
True}``; a URL is reduced to scheme and host by the writer, which sets ``secret``
when anything was removed. A value that is not text is stored as canonical JSON
text (:func:`_audit_change_text`); ``before`` and ``after`` are cut to 500
characters.
AuditChange.title: AuditChange

AuditClient.description:
Where a request-driven audit row came from (SPEC §4.5.3, personal data, D9).

``ip`` is believed from a forwarded header only when the socket peer is a named
trusted proxy, and then only the rightmost entry (``ip_source="trusted_proxy"``);
otherwise it is the socket peer (``ip_source="peer"``) whatever the caller sent.
``ip`` is always a parsed address or ``None`` (:func:`normalise_audit_ip`): it is
mapped as Elasticsearch type ``ip``, which refuses the whole row for ``""`` or a
non-address such as a Unix-socket peer. ``peer`` keeps the raw socket address as
text. ``forwarded_for`` keeps the raw header as untrusted text, never used to
filter or group. Values are bounded on write.
AuditClient.title: AuditClient

AuditCount.description: ``GET /api/audit/count``: exact up to the requested cap, then ``gte``.
AuditCount.title: AuditCount

AuditPage.description:
``GET /api/audit`` (SPEC §4.5.10). ``records`` and ``total`` keep the old
``AuditListResponse`` keys so existing clients keep working. ``total`` is exact
when ``total_relation`` is ``eq`` and a lower bound when it is ``gte``.
``run_totals`` gives, for every ``run_id`` on this page, the run's event count
under the same filters, so a group split across pages says "6 of 10 steps".
AuditPage.title: AuditPage

AuditRecord.description:
One audit row as the read API returns it (SPEC §4.5.10): the stored
:class:`AuditDoc` fields, the Round 14 fields when the row carries them (absent on
legacy rows, never shown empty) and the read-time projections.

Read leniently: a stored row is never rejected because a value drifted. An
unknown ``action_type`` keeps its token (it is categorised as System, never
hidden); an invalid Round 14 value is dropped as not recorded. ``outcome`` and
``actor_type`` may be derived for a legacy row, which ``*_derived`` says.
``category`` and ``event_label`` come from ``audit/event_categories.json``. Every
value renders as plain text (#9); ``prompt_excerpt`` and ``tool_output_summary``
carry fenced untrusted log data.
AuditRecord.title: AuditRecord

AuditRetention.description:
How long the deployment keeps the audit log, for the page's scope line. A
volatile store keeps it in memory only (lost on restart).
AuditRetention.title: AuditRetention

AuditTarget.description:
What an audit row acted on: ``{type, id, label, revision}`` (SPEC §4.5.3,
§3.6). ``label`` is the human name at the time (a case number, a dashboard name)
and is plain data. ``revision`` is the store revision the write creates, written
by ``audited_write`` on the action row BEFORE the store write: if the process
stops between the two, a reader can see that the named revision never existed
(the documented crash limit). ``None`` for targets without a revision.
AuditTarget.title: AuditTarget

AutoClosePolicy.description:
Operator-configured auto-close policy, one entry per verdict class.

Conservative defaults: FALSE_POSITIVE may auto-close above a bar; TRUE_POSITIVE
auto-close is OFF by default (an explicit, supported opt-in); NEEDS_HUMAN never
auto-closes (enforced in code regardless of this value).
AutoClosePolicy.title: AutoClosePolicy

AvatarBody.description: Thin set/clear of just the avatar (empty string clears it).
AvatarBody.title: AvatarBody

BrandingConfig.description:
Operator-customisable branding/appearance (UI-editable, persisted).

Powers the org logo + name + accent colour + theme shown across the console
shell (and the login screen). The logo is stored as a small base64 data URL
(bounded) so it round-trips through the config store with no asset hosting.
Non-secret; readable pre-auth so the login screen can show the org's brand.
BrandingConfig.title: BrandingConfig

BudgetConfig.description:
LLM cost-budget ceiling (Round 3 cost governance). When ``enabled`` the gate
compares rolling
spend (from the existing usage/cost ledger) against ``daily_usd``/``monthly_usd``;
at ``soft_warn_pct`` of a ceiling it WARNS, and ``on_exceed`` decides whether
crossing a ceiling merely warns or BLOCKS further LLM spend. NOTE: a budget block
affects whether an investigation RUNS — it never alters the close/escalate decision
of a case that DID run (#3).

Defaults ON as the Autopilot spend BACKSTOP: ``enabled=True`` + a bounded
``daily_usd=10`` (industry-grounded balanced default; ~20-40 Opus investigations —
see ``STANDARDS.md``) + ``soft_warn_pct=0.8`` + **``on_exceed='block'``**. A block
happens before the provider call and routes the case to NEEDS_HUMAN; it never closes
or discards the case (#3/#4). This is the backstop that keeps "read everything by
default" from becoming "spend everything." An operator can raise ``daily_usd``,
disable it, or explicitly choose warning-only mode. The ``autopilot_profile`` dial scales
``daily_usd`` (conservative $5 / balanced $10 / aggressive $50).
BudgetConfig.title: BudgetConfig

A :class:`CaseAction` applied to many cases at once. ``ids`` is the set of
target case ids; the action/payload fields are inherited verbatim so a bulk move
is IDENTICAL to N single-case moves.

The disposition is applied either way; this flag is what makes it independent analyst evidence rather than a value echoed back from the model-derived disposition already stored on the case.

escalation_level.title: Escalated compatibility flag

The disposition is applied either way; this flag is what makes it independent analyst evidence rather than a value echoed back from the model-derived disposition already stored on the case.
disposition_declared.title: The analyst chose this disposition in this action

level.description: Deprecated compatibility input for older clients. The case enters the single Escalated state; operator surfaces do not display numbered tiers.

CaseAutomationRule.description:
One post-decision threshold-automation rule (Wave 6 / F10).

RENAMED in Round 4 from ``AutomationRule`` → ``CaseAutomationRule`` to free the
``AutomationRule`` name for a future unified rule shape; a module-level
``AutomationRule = CaseAutomationRule`` alias (below ``ThresholdAutomationConfig``)
keeps every existing import + the stored ``threshold_automation`` config
round-tripping BYTE-IDENTICALLY (the wire key and ALL field names are unchanged).

Evaluated AFTER the deterministic ``case_manager.decide()`` + save. A rule
MATCHES a case when ALL of its present (non-empty) ``conditions`` hold, and
fires its single ``action``. The action is ADVISORY/SAFE
(``tag``/``recommend``/``notify``/``run_playbook``) — applied directly + audited
— OR ``request_approval``, which creates a HITL ``Proposal`` (the existing
proposer/approve path is the only live-write route). It can NEVER set
``case.status``/``disposition`` (#3). ``priority`` orders evaluation (lower =
earlier); ``conditions`` keys are matched leniently (an absent key never
constrains). ``payload`` carries action-specific data (e.g. the tag text, the
recommendation, the channel id, the ``playbook_id`` to run).
CaseAutomationRule.title: CaseAutomationRule

CaseComment.description:
An append-only analyst comment on a case (collaboration). ``author``/``body``
are user input — render-escaped in the UI, never trusted as prompt instructions.
CaseComment.title: CaseComment

CaseListResponse.description:
The paged case-list envelope. ``cases`` is the full ``Case`` model list (the
same shape ``Case.model_dump(mode='json')`` produced before typing).
CaseListResponse.title: CaseListResponse

CaseRunbooks.description:
``GET /api/cases/{case_id}/runbooks`` (SPEC §4.10.15a): the case's runs with
evidence redacted per viewer by the lookup grants, progress per run, the newer
published version per run, the free-form case tasks ("Other tasks") and the case
document's CAS revision.
CaseRunbooks.title: CaseRunbooks

CaseStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a case (Section 7.1). DECISION is deterministic code.

Two-axis model (see docs/research/.../STATUS_TAXONOMY.md): this is the
LIFECYCLE axis; the investigative outcome is the separate :class:`Disposition`.
The three ORIGINAL string values (``open``/``needs_human``/``closed``) are kept
BYTE-FOR-BYTE so stored cases load unchanged and ``decide()`` (#3) is untouched;
the richer states below are ADDED additively and reached via analyst lifecycle
actions + the existing ``escalate`` flag — never by rewriting the deterministic
decision. ``NEEDS_HUMAN`` is a RETAINED, deprecated alias of "open · awaiting
analyst" (the UI renders it that way).
CaseStatus.title: CaseStatus

CaseTask.description:
One checklist item / task on a case (Round 3 collaboration). ``status`` tracks
open→done; ``order`` keeps a stable manual ordering; ``logs`` is an append-only
note trail ``[{ts, by, note}]``. ``title``/``logs`` are plain data (#9).
CaseTask.title: CaseTask

ChatActiveTurn.description:
``GET /api/chat/turns/active`` (SPEC D13): one of the caller's running turns.
``label`` is an engine template, never model or log text.
ChatActiveTurn.title: ChatActiveTurn

ChatBudgetInfo.description: The daily budget the meter's ring measures against. ``models:read`` only.
ChatBudgetInfo.title: ChatBudgetInfo

ChatCatchUp.description:
"Since {since_label}: clause, clause and clause." (at most 160 characters as a
whole line; the server drops clauses from the end until it fits).
ChatCatchUp.title: ChatCatchUp

ChatCatchUpClause.description:
One clause of the catch-up line ("5 new cases (2 critical)") and the starter
it sends when clicked (action ``send`` only; SPEC §3.6).
ChatCatchUpClause.title: ChatCatchUpClause

ChatClarify.description:
A clarifying question the model asked instead of guessing (SPEC D10). Option
text is model-authored and may echo log values: the UI renders it as untrusted
text, and a pick is sent with ``origin="clarify"`` (follow_up taint class, #9).
ChatClarify.title: ChatClarify

ChatContext.description:
On-screen context snapshot the global chat flyout may attach (Feature 1).

ALL fields optional + best-effort. ``query``/``selection`` are
attacker-influenceable and MUST be fenced as UNTRUSTED in prompts; the context
is used only to DEFAULT the es_query tool (data view / time range), never as
instructions.
ChatContext.title: ChatContext

ChatContextBounds.description: The §4.2 bounds the meter and the run log display (no internal_domains).
ChatContextBounds.title: ChatContextBounds

ChatContextInfo.description:
``GET /api/chat/context`` (SPEC §8): everything the composer meter needs.
Money and budget fields are present only with ``models:read``; ``spent_today`` /
``remaining`` additionally need ``cost:view``. Without them the meter shows
tokens only plus ``budget_state``.
ChatContextInfo.title: ChatContextInfo

ChatConversationMatch.description: Where a ``?q=`` search hit a conversation (SPEC §7.5 Search).
ChatConversationMatch.title: ChatConversationMatch

ChatConversationMessage.description:
One durable Workspace-chat message.

``response`` keeps the bounded structured result needed to restore tables,
query links, cost and memory feedback.  It is plain JSON presentation data;
the authoritative chat engine still receives only ``role`` + ``content`` as
prior model history.
ChatConversationMessage.title: ChatConversationMessage

ChatConversationPage.description:
``GET /api/chat/conversations``: one page of the caller's conversation
summaries. With ``?q=`` each row also carries ``match {message_id, snippet}``
(rows of a plain listing omit it; the route serialises with
``response_model_exclude_unset`` so the wire shape is unchanged).
ChatConversationPage.title: ChatConversationPage

ChatConversationSearchHit.description: A conversation summary returned by a content search (never persisted).
ChatConversationSearchHit.title: ChatConversationSearchHit

ChatConversationUpdateRequest.description:
``PATCH /api/chat/conversations/{id}`` (SPEC §7.5 Pin): rename and/or pin.
At least one field is required; pinning never changes ``updated_at``.
ChatConversationUpdateRequest.title: ChatConversationUpdateRequest

ChatEntityQuestion.description: The server-worded question for one entity (sent with ``origin: "starter"``).
ChatEntityQuestion.title: ChatEntityQuestion

ChatEntityRef.description: ``POST /api/chat/entity-question`` body: what an Ask AI chip asks about.
ChatEntityRef.title: ChatEntityRef

ChatFeedbackEntryOut.description: One of the caller's own ratings.
ChatFeedbackEntryOut.title: ChatFeedbackEntryOut

ChatFeedbackRequest.description:
``POST /api/chat/feedback`` (SPEC §3.2). Stored per user and audited; never used
to train a model.
ChatFeedbackRequest.title: ChatFeedbackRequest

ChatFeedbackSummary.description:
``GET /api/chat/feedback/summary``: the caller's ratings as aggregates only
(never a comment or which answer). ``down_by_reason`` holds every reason, zero
included; ``since`` echoes the filter.
ChatFeedbackSummary.title: ChatFeedbackSummary

ChatMessagePage.description:
``GET /api/chat/conversations/{id}/messages``: messages oldest first, each
restored to its full text, and how many older ones remain
(``earlier_message_count``; 0 = this page starts the conversation).
ChatMessagePage.title: ChatMessagePage

ChatPrompt.description:
One saved composer prompt (chat revamp SPEC §10.4). Plain user text: rendered
as text, sent as an ordinary user message (it is the user's own words).

Round 12 prompt library (SPEC §3.1): an optional ``category`` and a ``favorite``
star; ``{name}`` placeholders in ``text`` are filled in by the composer before
sending (client-side; the server stores the template as plain text).
ChatPrompt.title: ChatPrompt

ChatReportSaveError.description:
Why the report a chat answer asked for was NOT saved (SPEC D11; additive). The
answer itself is saved; ``message`` is a server template, never model text.
``retryable``: the same save may work later (a store outage), so the UI can offer
"Save as report"; a full library or an answer with nothing to save cannot.

``title`` and ``template`` (additive) record what the answer's header asked for, so
"Save as report" (``POST /api/reports/from-answer``) saves the SAME report the server
could not; the server reads them from the stored answer, never from the client.
``title`` is model-derived display text (#9); both are lenient on replay.
ChatReportSaveError.title: ChatReportSaveError

ChatSavedReport.description:
The report the server saved from this answer (SPEC D11). Created by the server
from the persisted message, never by the model. ``skipped`` (additive): sections
of the answer that did not fit the report's item or size limit.
ChatSavedReport.title: ChatSavedReport

ChatStarter.description:
One starter card (SPEC §10.5; Round 13 SPEC-chat §3.2.1).

``id`` is the FAMILY id (one card per family; the pre-Round-13 ids investigate,
hunt, posture, shift_brief, explain_metric and learn_app stay valid). ``label`` is
a short family name and ``description`` equals ``reason``, for older clients. For
action ``send``, ``prompt`` is both the visible question and the exact text the
client sends with ``origin: "starter"`` (never edited, never put in the composer);
dynamic templates render at most 100 characters. Action ``open_conversation`` and
``use_prompt`` cards are display-only: ``prompt`` is their card text (at most 120
characters) and is never sent; ``ref`` names the conversation or saved prompt.
ChatStarter.title: ChatStarter

ChatStarterEvent.description:
``POST /api/chat/starters/events`` body (SPEC §3.2.2, §3.6). Presentation state
only: it updates the caller's own starter state document, writes no audit row and
stores no text (D10). A ``thread`` ``viewed`` event carries no keys.
ChatStarterEvent.title: ChatStarterEvent

ChatStarterRef.description:
A typed reference a starter names (a case, rule, source, campaign, ATT&CK
technique) or opens (a conversation, a saved prompt). ``value`` passes its kind's
strict grammar (``chat_starter_text.ref_value``) unchanged, or the model refuses it:
a value is never cut, quoted or altered (SPEC §3.8.1).
ChatStarterRef.title: ChatStarterRef

ChatStartersInfo.description:
``GET /api/chat/starters`` (SPEC §3.2.2). ``enabled`` mirrors
``chat_agent.dynamic_starters``; when it is false the server returns the evergreen
set only and no catch-up line. ``expires_at`` is ``as_of`` + 120 s.
ChatStartersInfo.title: ChatStartersInfo

ChatStep.description:
One row of a turn's run log (SPEC §3.3). Every string is engine-authored or
display-sanitised; ``untrusted_params`` and ``query`` may carry model/log-derived
values, which the UI renders as untrusted text/code and prompts fence.
ChatStep.title: ChatStep

ChatStepObservation.description:
``GET …/steps/{index}``: what the model saw for one lookup. ``observation`` is
the aggregate observation (never raw log rows); ``untrusted`` is always True —
its values come from logs and tools and are rendered as text. ``truncated``: the
stored copy was shortened structurally to fit its storage bound.
ChatStepObservation.title: ChatStepObservation

ChatStepProgress.description:
Progress of one long-running lookup (an exact aggregate scan). ``total`` is None
when the store cannot say up front; ``unit`` is a display noun ("cases").
ChatStepProgress.title: ChatStepProgress

ChatStreamEventModel.description:
A named wrapper so the discriminated union appears in ``openapi.json`` as one
component (``/chat/stream`` documents each NDJSON line with this schema).
ChatStreamEventModel.title: ChatStreamEventModel

ChatToolInfo.description: One row of the caller's tool catalogue ("What can the assistant access?").
ChatToolInfo.title: ChatToolInfo

ChatTopicQuestion.description:
``GET /api/chat/topics/{topic_id}`` (SPEC §10.7 "Ask about this"): the
templated question for a console_map topic. The page sends this text with
``origin="starter"``; it never sends free text of its own for a topic.
ChatTopicQuestion.title: ChatTopicQuestion

Citation.description:
A source the answer cites by id (``D1`` doc, ``C2`` case, ``K3`` knowledge,
``M1`` ATT&CK, ``Q1`` query). The model references ids only; the server resolves
them; the client re-validates every target.
Citation.title: Citation

ColumnState.description:
Per-table column layout the user customised: the ordered column ids, the
hidden column ids, and a ``widths`` map (column id → pixel width). A table that
has no stored ColumnState renders its built-in default — this only ever ADDS an
override, never removes a column from existence.
ColumnState.title: ColumnState

ConnectorTestRequest.description: Test the exact saved or draft source configuration without persisting it.
ConnectorTestRequest.title: ConnectorTestRequest

ConsoleLink.description:
A console destination resolved from ``console_map`` (never from model text).
``allowed`` comes from the caller's grants; a disallowed link renders as plain
text naming the grant it ``requires``.
ConsoleLink.title: ConsoleLink

CustomRoleBody.description:
A custom-role definition submitted for create/update. Mirrors
:class:`app.models.CustomRole`; validated + cleaned server-side.
CustomRoleBody.title: CustomRoleBody

CustomizationConfig.description:
ORG-level pervasive-customization defaults (Wave 7, admin-edited).

This is the ORG side of the two-store customization model: the defaults every
user inherits unless they override them in their PERSONAL UserPrefs bucket. The
cascade resolver merges ORG ← USER (a user override always wins). Admin-only via
the dedicated ``/api/prefs/org`` + ``/api/terminology`` routes (and the settings
PUT). All free-text is PLAIN DATA rendered by the UI — a terminology label or a
saved-view name is NEVER interpolated unfenced into an LLM prompt (#9).

* ``terminology`` — label overrides, e.g. ``{"case": "incident", "cases":
  "incidents"}``. The UI ``t(key)`` helper falls back to the built-in default
  string for any key not present here. Bounded per-key + total size (below).
* ``default_saved_views`` — org-shared saved views (the operator's curated list
  configurations); a user may clone one into their personal set.
* ``default_theme`` — the org default colour mode for a user who has not chosen
  their own (a user's ``UserPrefs.theme_mode`` overrides this).
* ``default_pinned_view_ids`` — org-default pinned (quick-access) saved-view ids.
* ``default_dashboards`` — org/role default custom-dashboard layouts (Round 5 / G7),
  keyed by role (or ``"default"``). Each value is a ``DashboardLayout`` serialised as
  a plain dict (kept loose here to avoid a config→models import cycle — the same
  pattern ``default_saved_views`` uses). The FE clone-to-customize flow copies the
  caller's role default into their PERSONAL set on first edit. A dashboard layout is
  ADVISORY presentation state only — it never feeds ``case_manager.decide()`` (#3),
  and every dashboard/widget ``name``/``title`` is PLAIN data the UI render-escapes
  (#9), never interpolated unfenced into a prompt.
CustomizationConfig.title: CustomizationConfig

DashboardLayoutIn.description:
The create and update request body of a personal board (``POST
/api/dashboards``, ``PUT /api/dashboards/{id}``): :class:`DashboardLayout` with the
Round 14 fields validated strictly, so a bad ``default_window`` or
``derived_from`` is refused at the write boundary instead of being dropped.
DashboardLayoutIn.title: DashboardLayoutIn

DashboardWidget.description:
One placed widget on a custom dashboard (Round 5 / G7). The geometry fields
(``i``/``x``/``y``/``w``/``h``/``minW``/``minH``/``static``) ARE the
``react-grid-layout`` item shape: 12-column absolute grid coordinates the RGL
edit surface reads/writes verbatim, so the persistence schema and the layout
library share one contract (no adapter). ``i`` is the stable item id used both
as the RGL key AND the widget instance id.

``type`` selects a widget from the client widget registry (a WidgetType enum
value, kept a str so an unknown/legacy type round-trips and is dropped by the
client's reconcile-on-load); ``options`` is the widget's declarative config
(title, series, source id, …) — small free-form PLAIN data the UI
render-escapes (#9), NEVER interpolated unfenced into a prompt. A widget layout
is ADVISORY presentation only — it never feeds ``case_manager.decide()`` (#3).
DashboardWidget.title: DashboardWidget

DataExportArchiveRequest.description: Selected safe scopes for one server-assembled full-history ZIP.
DataExportArchiveRequest.title: DataExportArchiveRequest

DataExportRequest.description: Selectable export request. ``all`` expands to every safe application scope.
DataExportRequest.title: DataExportRequest

DataExportSegmentCancelRequest.description: Release a still-open point-in-time cursor after operator cancellation.
DataExportSegmentCancelRequest.title: DataExportSegmentCancelRequest

DataExportSegmentRequest.description: One bounded continuation segment of a complete, scope-specific export.
DataExportSegmentRequest.title: DataExportSegmentRequest

DecisionOption.description:
One option of a Decision step. ``marks_not_applicable`` names later step ids
this option skips (only steps still To do).
DecisionOption.title: DecisionOption

DiscoverLink.description: Payload the plugin feeds to Kibana's locators API (Section 8.1).
DiscoverLink.title: DiscoverLink

Disposition.description:
Investigative OUTCOME (verdict-class) axis — the analyst-confirmable,
reportable classification on/after close. Orthogonal to :class:`CaseStatus`
(lifecycle). Defaulted to ``None`` on the Case so old stored cases load
unchanged; the LLM ``Verdict`` is unchanged and still feeds ``decide()``.
Disposition.title: Disposition

FeedbackEntry.description:
An analyst's grade of an AI verdict on a case (the eval / quality loop,
Vigil-inspired). Append-only on the case; aggregated by /api/feedback/stats to
measure agreement rate, grading quality, outcome mix and time saved.
FeedbackEntry.title: FeedbackEntry

FeedbackOutcome.description:
Human-confirmed outcome accepted by the analyst feedback endpoint.

This is deliberately broader than :class:`Disposition`: evaluation can record a
true/false negative even when that classification is not a live case disposition.
Keeping the vocabulary here makes the HTTP contract explicit and prevents arbitrary
strings from silently becoming tuner ground truth.
FeedbackOutcome.title: FeedbackOutcome

HealthResponse.description:
The public health envelope (also read by the webui to detect an in-memory
store, ``store_type``).

``es_connected`` is a compatibility-stable alias that historically named the
only supported state backend. New clients must use ``state_store_connected``;
both fields deliberately carry the same own-state readiness result.

degraded.description: Whether a subsystem the product depends on is impaired while the state store itself is reachable. Additive: `status` keeps its historical meaning (state-store readiness) so existing clients are unaffected.
degraded.title: Degraded

degraded_reasons.description: Opaque, closed-vocabulary codes naming each active degradation. This endpoint is PUBLIC, so it carries no counts, source names or posture detail — the authenticated /api/diagnostics/health surface owns those.
degraded_reasons.title: Degraded Reasons

es_connected.description: Compatibility alias for state_store_connected; this does not describe log-source Elasticsearch connectivity.
es_connected.title: Es Connected

state_backend.description: Configured owned-state backend: elasticsearch, postgres, or sqlite.
state_backend.title: State Backend

state_store_connected.description: Whether the selected owned-state backend passed its write-path probe.
state_store_connected.title: State Store Connected

HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse

InvestigateRequest.description:
Start an investigation. Provide either a known cluster signature/case, or an
ad-hoc entity + event ids (Surface 2 row click).
InvestigateRequest.title: InvestigateRequest

JobProgress.description: Bounded progress projection shared by Jobs, Inbox, SSE, and the Console.
JobProgress.title: JobProgress

JobPublic.description: Secret-free/self-scoped wire projection returned by the Jobs API and SSE.
JobPublic.title: JobPublic

JobStatus.description: Durable lifecycle of a server-owned operator job.
JobStatus.title: JobStatus

LookupResult.description:
The stored result of one lookup run (SPEC §4.10.7, §4.10.8). Every value is
untrusted plain text (#9). ``params`` are the resolved values; ``ran_by`` is
``agentic_soc`` for a background ``on_attach`` run or the person who pressed Run.
``table`` is ``{columns <= 6, rows <= 20, cells <= 200 chars}``: an ``aggregate``
table holds counts per key; a ``rows`` table holds raw ``log_search`` rows,
shown to people only and reduced by code to a row count and top values before
any prompt (#7). ``window_clamped`` says ``window_to`` was cut to ``ran_at``.
LookupResult.title: LookupResult

LookupTemplate.description:
A declarative, read-only lookup a Lookup step runs (SPEC §4.10.8). ``filter``
maps a field (validated against the evidence-fields grammar) to a literal or one
``{{template value}}``, at most 8 entries; ``group_by`` (``log_stats`` only) at
most 2 fields; ``indicator`` (``enrich`` only) one template value. The window
spans at most 30 days; ``log_search`` returns at most 20 rows.
LookupTemplate.title: LookupTemplate

MatchExplanation.description:
Why a runbook was chosen (SPEC §4.10.4). ``tier`` is 3 (rule matched), 2
(technique matched, the runbook names no rules), 1 (other criteria only) or 0 (the
fallback). ``tie`` says a tie survived to the id rule.
MatchExplanation.title: MatchExplanation

MatchPreview.description:
``POST /api/runbooks/match-preview`` (SPEC §4.10.15a): which of the last 500
cases in 30 days the definition would get. Nothing is attached and no metric
changes. ``truncated`` says a list was cut at 50; ``counts`` are always exact.
MatchPreview.title: MatchPreview

MatchPreviewCase.description: A case the previewed runbook would get, with why.
MatchPreviewCase.title: MatchPreviewCase

MatchPreviewCounts.description: Exact group sizes; each list above holds at most 50.
MatchPreviewCounts.title: MatchPreviewCounts

MatchPreviewNearMiss.description: A case that nearly matched, with the criteria that failed.
MatchPreviewNearMiss.title: MatchPreviewNearMiss

MatchPreviewOther.description: A case another runbook would win, naming the winner.
MatchPreviewOther.title: MatchPreviewOther

MatchedCriterion.description: A criterion that matched, and the case value that matched it.
MatchedCriterion.title: MatchedCriterion

MemoryListResponse.description:
The operator-memory list envelope. Each entry is a loose typed dict
(text/category/tags/source/active/…) rendered PLAIN by the UI (#9).
MemoryListResponse.title: MemoryListResponse

MemoryProposal.description:
A memory change the MODEL proposed (§4.8). Never executed by the engine: the
UI confirms it through the existing memory routes under ``memory:manage``.
``remove`` takes exact entry ids only (no text matching from chat).
MemoryProposal.title: MemoryProposal

MemorySuggestion.description:
A durable fact the chat agent NOTICED and proposes to remember. The UI shows
it for the analyst to confirm before it is saved — the agent never auto-saves a
suggestion (only explicit "remember: …" commands are executed).
MemorySuggestion.title: MemorySuggestion

MetricsBreakdown.description:
``GET /api/metrics/breakdown`` (SPEC §4.4.2): exact case or usage counts by one
or two fields over a window, from the same engine as the chat's ``case_stats``,
so dashboards and chat agree on every number. ``exact`` is false and ``partial``
true when a store failure cut the scan (the figures are then lower bounds, said
so by the widget). ``multi_valued`` warns that rows do not sum to ``total``.
``missing_created`` counts the matching records with no readable creation time
(cases) or timestamp (usage), never silently dropped; ``missing_in_total`` says
whether ``total`` holds them (all time: yes, in the "no date" bucket; a bounded
window cannot place them).
MetricsBreakdown.title: MetricsBreakdown

MetricsBreakdownBucket.description:
One zero-filled calendar bucket of a bucketed breakdown, in order. When ``top``
cut groups, ``other_count`` is this bucket's share of ``other`` (``count``, or
``calls`` for usage), so the bucket's listed groups plus it are the bucket's total;
``None`` when nothing was cut.
MetricsBreakdownBucket.title: MetricsBreakdownBucket

MetricsBreakdownGroup.description:
One row of a breakdown. ``key`` is the ``by`` value (``None`` is the empty
group, for example the unassigned cases); ``then_key`` the ``then`` value;
``bucket`` the zero-filled calendar bucket label. Keys are untrusted plain
strings (rule ids, source names, technique names). Case metrics are filled for
``kind=cases`` and ``None`` for ``kind=usage``; ``calls`` and ``cost_usd`` the
other way round (for usage ``count`` equals ``calls``).
MetricsBreakdownGroup.title: MetricsBreakdownGroup

MetricsBreakdownOther.description: The exact remainder past ``top``: how many records and how many groups.
MetricsBreakdownOther.title: MetricsBreakdownOther

MissedCriterion.description: A criterion that failed: what the runbook expects and what the case has.
MissedCriterion.title: MissedCriterion

ModelConfig.description:
Per-role model selection. Routed through the single gateway.

``base_url``/``api_version``/``region`` are Round 3 Wave 2b ADDITIVE, optional
endpoint overrides (all default None → today's behaviour is byte-identical). They
let a per-role assignment pin its own endpoint without depending on the bundled
``model_registry.json``:

* ``base_url`` — an OpenAI-compatible / Azure-resource / Bedrock-runtime endpoint
  (vLLM/Ollama/OpenRouter/Together/Groq, or ``https://<resource>.openai.azure.com``).
  When unset the gateway falls back to ``base_url_for(model)`` from the registry,
  then the provider's default endpoint — so existing configs are unaffected.
* ``api_version`` — the Azure OpenAI ``api-version`` query param for this model.
* ``region`` — the cloud region (e.g. Bedrock ``us-east-1``).
ModelConfig.title: ModelConfig

prompt.default: Reply with the single word: ok
prompt.title: Prompt

NotificationPrefBody.description:
The PUT body for a user's own notification prefs (the ``user`` field is forced
to the requester server-side — a caller can never write another user's bucket).
NotificationPrefBody.title: NotificationPrefBody

NotificationProvidersResponse.description:
The notification providers catalog envelope (no secrets, names and ids only).

``channel_types`` holds the registered channel type ids as plain strings, the
shape ``notifications.channel.channel_types()`` returns (``["email", "slack",
...]``). Typing it as a list of objects made the response validation fail, so
the route answered 500 instead of the catalog.
NotificationProvidersResponse.title: NotificationProvidersResponse

ObservedStableRelease.description:
Untrusted discovery hint safe to show before signed preflight.

The public projection intentionally omits repository/artifact URLs, commit and
image digests, and component coordinates.  It is not an install authority.
ObservedStableRelease.title: ObservedStableRelease

PrecedentBootstrapRequest.description: An explicit, honest ratification of MODEL verdicts as weak precedent.

acknowledgement.description: Must be exactly: I am ratifying model verdicts, not independent analyst ground truth
acknowledgement.title: Acknowledgement

PrecedentBootstrapRequest.title: PrecedentBootstrapRequest

PrecedentExclusionRequest.description:
Exclude one or more cases from the precedent corpus.

Supply ``case_ids`` directly, or ``select`` a population by the projection's OWN
metadata keys. Free-text rule-title matching is deliberately NOT offered: a title is
content, and a detection-content update rewrites it underneath a saved selection.
PrecedentExclusionRequest.title: PrecedentExclusionRequest

PrecedentRepairRequest.description:
Re-render stored precedent from the CURRENT builder and rewrite what drifted.

There is no selector here, and that is the design. No metadata key records which
generation of the builder produced a chunk's text, so the ONLY honest selector is
to render each case again through the same projector the projection uses and
compare the two strings. A free-text selector over chunk TEXT would be strictly
worse than the free-text metadata selector this module already refuses: precedent
text carries the analyst note, the model's recommended action and log-derived
evidence summaries, so matching prose means matching attacker- and
operator-influenceable content (#9).
PrecedentRepairRequest.title: PrecedentRepairRequest

ProposalBulkRejectRequest.description: Explicit ids plus one audited reason for clearing a review queue.
ProposalBulkRejectRequest.title: ProposalBulkRejectRequest

ProviderSecretsBody.description:
Map of ``secret_key -> value`` (value=None/"" clears). Only keys the provider's
manifest declares are accepted; unknown keys are rejected (400).
ProviderSecretsBody.title: ProviderSecretsBody

RagDocumentsResponse.description:
The RAG corpus document-list envelope. Each document is a loose typed dict
(title/source/chunk_count/…) rendered PLAIN by the UI (#9).
RagDocumentsResponse.title: RagDocumentsResponse

ReinvestigateRequest.description:
Re-run the investigation on an existing case. Optional ``model`` overrides
the investigation-role models (router/investigator/formatter) for THIS run via a
prefs copy (the per-call model-override technique) — no gateway plumbing change.
ReinvestigateRequest.title: ReinvestigateRequest

RelatedBatchJobPublic.description: Bounded, provider-secret-free LLM Batch summary on the unified Jobs view.
RelatedBatchJobPublic.title: RelatedBatchJobPublic

Report.description: A per-user report document (SPEC §9.1): <= 40 items, strict-CAS ``version``.
Report.title: Report

ReportAddRequest.description:
``POST /api/reports/add``: add BY REFERENCE. The server loads the block (or the
whole answer as a ``section`` when ``block_id`` is absent) from the caller-owned
persisted Workspace message and snapshots it; client-supplied block JSON is never
accepted, so case-scoped content cannot be added by construction.
ReportAddRequest.title: ReportAddRequest

ReportAddResponse.title: ReportAddResponse

ReportFromAnswerRequest.description:
``POST /api/reports/from-answer``: "Save as report" for one caller-owned
Workspace answer whose header-requested report could not be saved (D11). Nothing
else is client-supplied: the title and template the answer asked for are read
from the stored answer, and the content is resolved from it like every add.
ReportFromAnswerRequest.title: ReportFromAnswerRequest

ReportFromConversationRequest.description:
``POST /api/reports/from-conversation``: save a whole Workspace conversation as
a new report (each answer one section). ``idempotency_key`` makes a retry return
the same report.
ReportFromConversationRequest.title: ReportFromConversationRequest

ReportFromConversationResponse.description:
The saved report, how many items it holds, how many answers did not fit
(``skipped``) and whether this call created it (False: an idempotent replay).
ReportFromConversationResponse.title: ReportFromConversationResponse

ReportItem.description: One report item: a validated block snapshot or a whole-answer section.
ReportItem.title: ReportItem

ReportItemScope.description: Scope captured server-side at add time (never client-supplied).
ReportItemScope.title: ReportItemScope

ReportItemSource.description: Where an item came from (a caller-owned persisted Workspace message).
ReportItemSource.title: ReportItemSource

ReportListEntry.description:
One row of the per-user report index (``GET /api/reports``).

``conversation_id`` names the conversation whose DRAFT this report is (at most one
per conversation); ``source_conversation_id`` names the conversation the report
came from (the one conversation all its items name, else the draft's), for the
library's "Source conversation" column. A report saved from an answer or a whole
conversation is never a draft, so it carries only the second. Rows written before
the field existed read ``None`` until the report next changes.
ReportListEntry.title: ReportListEntry

ReportPatchRequest.description:
``PATCH /api/reports/{id}``: title, template, item order, notes, removals —
all under ``expected_version`` (409 ``report_version_conflict`` on mismatch).
``item_order`` must be a permutation of the remaining item ids; ``notes`` maps
item id → note (``null`` clears it).
ReportPatchRequest.title: ReportPatchRequest

ReportSummary.description:
The AI-written executive summary (one gateway call over the §9.4 digest).
Stale when ``based_on_version`` lags the report's ``version``.
ReportSummary.title: ReportSummary

RolePreviewBody.description:
A DRAFT custom role to resolve (no persistence). Same shape as
:class:`CustomRoleBody`.
RolePreviewBody.title: RolePreviewBody

RuleCaseOutcomes.description:
The analyst-outcome family only (analyst-policy closes excluded); the AI
verdict family is never labelled as an analyst outcome.
RuleCaseOutcomes.title: RuleCaseOutcomes

RuleCaseRow.description: One of the newest cases from the rule (at most 5), named by case number.
RuleCaseRow.title: RuleCaseRow

RuleDefinition.description:
A config-driven, pre-baked-but-editable detection rule (C3-1).

Each definition classifies a raw event (via ``match``) into a named rule, can
carry its own ``correlation`` override and per-role ``model_override`` (C3-6b),
and is evaluated in ascending ``priority`` (then list order) so ModSec
sub-rules (lower priority) win over the generic ``modsec_audit_log`` rule.

``mitre``/``schedule``/``suppression`` are ADDITIVE, defaulted G6-editor metadata
(advisory only — none feeds ``decide()``, #3): ``mitre`` is a list of ATT&CK
technique ids the rule maps to (drives the coverage heatmap), ``schedule`` persists
an optional per-rule cadence intent, and ``suppression`` persists alert-storm
collapse intent (never a silent DROP — see :class:`RuleSuppression`).
RuleDefinition.title: RuleDefinition

RuleMatch.description:
A single field predicate used to classify a raw log into a detection rule.

``field`` is a dotted path read with the same tolerant ``dotted_get`` the rest
of the suite uses (handles nested objects AND flattened keys). Operators:

* ``equals``  — ``str(value-at-field) == value``
* ``prefix``  — ``str(value-at-field).startswith(value)``  (e.g. ModSec rule.id "941…")
* ``tag``     — ``value`` is a member of the field's list/array (e.g. rule.tags)
* ``exists``  — the field is present and non-empty
RuleMatch.title: RuleMatch

RuleSchedule.description:
Optional per-detection-rule schedule metadata (G6 R5 "Schedule" tab).

ADVISORY ONLY — the poller's durable per-feed cursor (``{source.id}:{feed.id}``)
owns the actual evaluation cadence today; these values persist the operator's
intent so the editor round-trips losslessly and a future per-rule scheduler can
honour them. It NEVER feeds ``case_manager.decide()`` (#3). Both fields default
None (== inherit the feed/global schedule), so an existing stored rule loads
byte-identically.
RuleSchedule.title: RuleSchedule

RuleSeverityPoint.description: One time bucket of a rule's alerts, counted per named level.
RuleSeverityPoint.title: RuleSeverityPoint

RuleSeveritySeries.description: Alerts over time by named level. ``bucket`` is the bucket width ("12h").
RuleSeveritySeries.title: RuleSeveritySeries

RuleSuiteDefinition.description: The summary of a suite detection rule (``Preferences.rule_catalog``).
RuleSuiteDefinition.title: RuleSuiteDefinition

RuleSummary.description:
``GET /api/rules/summary`` (SPEC §4.6.2): one rule's picture. Each section
checks its own grant and carries its own status, so the rule sheet degrades per
section. No model call (#6) and no raw rows (#7): the latest alerts come from
``GET /api/logs?rule=``. The rule value and every IP, host and title are
untrusted plain strings (#9).
RuleSummary.title: RuleSummary

RuleSummaryAlerts.description:
The alert figures. ``count_relation`` is ``gte`` when any source was sampled;
the Console then never names the count in "Open all N in Logs".
RuleSummaryAlerts.title: RuleSummaryAlerts

RuleSummaryAnalystPolicy.description: The operator's "declared benign" policy for the rule, or ``None``.
RuleSummaryAnalystPolicy.title: RuleSummaryAnalystPolicy

RuleSummaryCases.description: Cases whose ``rule_ids`` hold the rule, exact through ``case_aggregate``.
RuleSummaryCases.title: RuleSummaryCases

RuleSummaryDefinition.description:
Where the rule is defined: ``suite`` with its summary, or ``source`` meaning
"Defined in the source SIEM" (no settings link).
RuleSummaryDefinition.title: RuleSummaryDefinition

RuleSummarySource.description:
A source that contributed to the alert figures, and whether it could filter
on the rule exactly (``False``: counted from a bounded newest-N sample).
RuleSummarySource.title: RuleSummarySource

RuleSummaryTopList.description: A bounded top list (at most 10 rows); ``exact`` false when sampled.
RuleSummaryTopList.title: RuleSummaryTopList

RuleSummaryWindow.description: The window a rule summary measured: ``{label, from, to}`` (ISO UTC).
RuleSummaryWindow.title: RuleSummaryWindow

RuleSuppression.description:
Optional per-detection-rule alert-storm suppression metadata (G6 R5).

A DISTINCT concept from the ``correlation`` threshold (Elastic keeps them apart;
conflating them is a known analyst pitfall). ADVISORY/STORAGE ONLY today — this
persists the operator's intent so the Suppression editor round-trips; the engine
does NOT silently DROP events from this per-rule block. Any actual suppression that
would DROP a candidate stays a HITL Proposal via the existing
``Preferences.suppression_rules`` path (#3/#4-safe: never silently drops). All
fields are defaulted so a stored rule without it loads unchanged.
RuleSuppression.title: RuleSuppression

RuleTopRow.description: One row of a top list (an IP, a host or a user) with its count. Untrusted.
RuleTopRow.title: RuleTopRow

RunbookAppliesTo.description: The first rule and technique chips of a library row; ``more`` counts the rest.
RunbookAppliesTo.title: RunbookAppliesTo

RunbookAttachResult.description:
``POST /api/cases/{case_id}/runbooks``: the new run, or ``already_attached``
(idempotent per case and runbook, #4).
RunbookAttachResult.title: RunbookAttachResult

RunbookCandidate.description: One entry of the Start runbook picker (``GET .../runbooks/candidates``).
RunbookCandidate.title: RunbookCandidate

RunbookCandidates.description: The Start runbook picker list, best match first.
RunbookCandidates.title: RunbookCandidates

RunbookDefinition.description:
A runbook's canonical definition (SPEC §4.10.2). It has no ``version`` field:
a version is metadata of the stored document (``RunbookVersionDoc.version``) and
of a built-in's front matter. ``phases`` is ordered, 1 to 6, each used by at least
one step; ``steps`` holds 1 to 40. ``references`` are https links only, at most
10. ``review_every_days`` defaults to 180 (E6).
RunbookDefinition.title: RunbookDefinition

RunbookDetail.description:
``GET /api/runbooks/{id}`` (SPEC §4.10.15a). ``draft`` and ``in_review`` are
present only to a holder of ``runbooks:manage`` or ``runbooks:publish``.
``open_runs_by_version`` maps a version to the active runs pinned to it.
``revision`` is the library document's CAS revision, sent back as
``expected_revision``.
RunbookDetail.title: RunbookDetail

RunbookDiscardResult.description:
``DELETE /api/runbooks/{id}/draft``: the runbook after its draft is gone, or
``removed`` when it was never published (it disappears).
RunbookDiscardResult.title: RunbookDiscardResult

RunbookDraftBody.description: ``PUT /api/runbooks/{id}/draft``: the new draft and the revision it edits.
RunbookDraftBody.title: RunbookDraftBody

RunbookIssue.description:
One validation problem: where (``steps[3].lookup.filter``), a stable code and
a plain sentence naming the fix.
RunbookIssue.title: RunbookIssue

RunbookLibrary.description:
``GET /api/runbooks`` (the new shape): built-ins and operator runbooks. There
is no empty library: the 12 built-ins are always listed.
RunbookLibrary.title: RunbookLibrary

RunbookLookupTestBody.description:
``POST /api/runbooks/lookup-test``: run a draft lookup against one case,
read-only, storing nothing.
RunbookLookupTestBody.title: RunbookLookupTestBody

RunbookMetrics.description:
``GET /api/runbooks/metrics`` (SPEC §4.10.15a). ``partial`` is true when a
ledger month document reached its cap inside the window. Every figure states its
population and none claims a runbook caused a time change.
RunbookMetrics.title: RunbookMetrics

RunbookMetricsCohort.description: One response-time cohort: its size and median time to resolve.
RunbookMetricsCohort.title: RunbookMetricsCohort

RunbookMetricsCohorts.description: Cases with and without a completed run. A comparison, never a cause.
RunbookMetricsCohorts.title: RunbookMetricsCohorts

RunbookMetricsCoverage.description: Human-handled cases in the window, and how many had a run.
RunbookMetricsCoverage.title: RunbookMetricsCoverage

RunbookMetricsPhaseRow.description: The median time to finish one phase of one runbook.
RunbookMetricsPhaseRow.title: RunbookMetricsPhaseRow

RunbookMetricsRecentRun.description: One of the most recent runs, for the library's Recent runs panel.
RunbookMetricsRecentRun.title: RunbookMetricsRecentRun

RunbookMetricsRuleGap.description: A rule seen in the window that no Published runbook matches. Untrusted.
RunbookMetricsRuleGap.title: RunbookMetricsRuleGap

RunbookMetricsRunbookRow.description: Runs started, completed and abandoned for one runbook in the window.
RunbookMetricsRunbookRow.title: RunbookMetricsRunbookRow

RunbookMetricsStepRow.description: The median time and the skip count of one step.
RunbookMetricsStepRow.title: RunbookMetricsStepRow

RunbookMigratedFrom.description: The legacy document a migrated runbook came from (SPEC §4.10.17).
RunbookMigratedFrom.title: RunbookMigratedFrom

RunbookMigrationNotice.description:
The one-shot migration's counts (from its marker, §4.10.17), for the Runbooks
page's dismissible intro: "Your 10 procedures from the previous version are now
runbooks. 9 are published and due for review; 1 is a draft with problems to fix."
``None`` on the library response when nothing was migrated.
RunbookMigrationNotice.title: RunbookMigrationNotice

RunbookProgress.description:
Progress derived on read from a run (never stored). ``done`` counts only Done
steps; Not applicable is counted on its own and never as done. The chip reads
"4/11", "5/9 · 1 blocked" or "4/11 · 1 waiting".
RunbookProgress.title: RunbookProgress

RunbookProgressBody.description:
``POST /api/runbooks/progress``: progress for up to 100 cases at once, each id
1 to 128 characters (an id becomes part of a store key).
RunbookProgressBody.title: RunbookProgressBody

RunbookPublishBody.description:
``POST /api/runbooks/{id}/publish`` (SPEC §4.10.15): the version and the
library revision the publisher reviewed, both required. Publishing is the one
transition that makes runbook text trusted investigator guidance (#9), and drafts
are edited in place, so a publish is bound to exactly what was reviewed: a stale
``expected_revision`` answers ``409 runbook_conflict`` with the latest state.
``content_hash`` (the reviewed version's ``RunbookVersionDoc.content_hash``) also
binds it across a discard and re-create, where a new library document can repeat
an old revision number; when given, a different stored hash is ``409
runbook_conflict`` too. The Console always sends it.
RunbookPublishBody.title: RunbookPublishBody

RunbookRef.description: A pinned reference to one version of a runbook (``derived_from``).
RunbookRef.title: RunbookRef

RunbookRejectBody.description: ``POST /api/runbooks/{id}/reject``: back to draft with a reason.
RunbookRejectBody.title: RunbookRejectBody

RunbookReviewNote.description: A reviewer's note on a version (a rejection reason, a review comment).
RunbookReviewNote.title: RunbookReviewNote

RunbookRevisionBody.description:
``retire``, ``restore``, ``reviewed``, ``duplicate`` and ``versions/{n}/restore``:
the revision the action is based on (optional for the idempotent ones).
RunbookRevisionBody.title: RunbookRevisionBody

RunbookRun.description:
One runbook run on one case (SPEC §4.10.7). A run pins its version: the
``snapshot`` lets it render without the catalog, and "Switch to v5" is an
explicit, audited step. ``attached_reason`` is the match explanation
(:class:`MatchExplanation`) or ``{by: <user>, note}``. Completing or abandoning a
run never changes the case (#3); one run per case and runbook (#4).
RunbookRun.title: RunbookRun

RunbookRunUpdate.description:
The result of any write to one run: a step update, a lookup, an approval, an AI
draft or its confirmation, a version switch or an abandon. ``revision`` is the case
document's CAS revision after the write.
RunbookRunUpdate.title: RunbookRunUpdate

RunbookSourceBody.description:
``POST /api/runbooks`` (create a draft), ``/validate``, ``/import`` and
``/match-preview``: a definition, or Markdown source, or (match preview only) an
existing runbook id.

``content`` is the old write shape's key, accepted only so the route can tell
``{id, content}`` apart after validation: any request that sets it (``"content" in
model_fields_set``) answers ``410 runbooks_moved``, because an old-shape write
cannot be honoured without making unreviewed text trusted (#9, E14).

content.description: Legacy key of the old write shape; any value answers 410 runbooks_moved.
content.title: Content

RunbookSourceBody.title: RunbookSourceBody

RunbookStep.description:
One step (SPEC §4.10.2, §4.10.3). ``id`` is a slug unique in the runbook and
stable across versions. Checks are written as questions. ``instructions`` is
restricted Markdown for people (never part of the investigator prompt);
``focus``, ``escalate_if`` and ``benign_if`` are what the investigator reads.
``lookup`` is required on Lookup steps and absent elsewhere; ``options`` holds 2
to 6 options on Decision steps. ``approval_role`` is honoured only when step
approvals are on; ``target_minutes`` is shown, never enforced.
RunbookStep.title: RunbookStep

RunbookStepDraftResult.description:
``POST .../steps/{step_id}/draft``: the run with the step's new AI draft
(labelled "AI draft" until a person confirms it), or with ``dry_run=true`` only
the estimate of the one gateway call (#6).
RunbookStepDraftResult.title: RunbookStepDraftResult

RunbookStepUpdate.description:
``PATCH /api/cases/{case_id}/runbooks/{run_id}/steps/{step_id}``. A stale
``expected_revision`` is never retried (``409 runbook_conflict``). ``assignee``
sent as ``null`` clears the assignment; an absent key leaves it (the route reads
``model_fields_set``).
RunbookStepUpdate.title: RunbookStepUpdate

RunbookSuggestion.description:
``POST /api/cases/{case_id}/runbooks/suggest``: the AI's suggestion, which a
person must select (it is never attached), or with ``dry_run=true`` only the
estimate of the one gateway call (#6).
RunbookSuggestion.title: RunbookSuggestion

RunbookSummary.description:
One library row (SPEC §4.10.15a). ``state`` is the most advanced visible
state. ``runs_30d`` is ``None`` without ``cases:read``. ``review_due_at`` is
``last_reviewed_at + review_every_days``; imported content is due at once (D38).
``replaced_by`` names the Published operator copy that stopped a built-in
matching. Titles and summaries are plain text.
RunbookSummary.title: RunbookSummary

RunbookValidation.description:
``POST /api/runbooks/validate``: the issues and the investigator guidance
length against its budget. Nothing is written.
RunbookValidation.title: RunbookValidation

RunbookVersionBody.description:
``POST /api/runbooks/{id}/submit``: the version sent for review. Publishing
takes :class:`RunbookPublishBody`, which requires the revision.
RunbookVersionBody.title: RunbookVersionBody

RunbookVersionDoc.description:
One immutable version (SPEC §4.10.5, §4.10.15a). ``content_hash`` is the
SHA-256 of the canonical definition; ``source`` its Markdown; ``prompt_chars`` the
investigator rendering's length (the budget is 3,000, E10).
RunbookVersionDoc.title: RunbookVersionDoc

RunbookVersionListItem.description: One row of a runbook's version history.
RunbookVersionListItem.title: RunbookVersionListItem

SavedView.description:
A named, reusable list configuration (filters + sort + optional columns) for
a UI surface (``cases``/``sources``/…). ``owner`` records who created it;
``shared`` marks an org-shared view (org defaults live on Preferences, but a
user may clone one into their personal set). ``filters`` is a small free-form
dict the frontend interprets; ``sort`` is e.g. ``"-created_at"``; ``columns``
optionally pins the visible/ordered column ids for the view. All free-text is
plain data (#9).
SavedView.title: SavedView

SavedViewBody.description:
Create/clone a personal saved view. ``id`` is server-assigned on create. All
free-text is plain data (#9).
SavedViewBody.title: SavedViewBody

SavedViewPatchBody.description: Partial edit of a personal saved view (only provided fields change).

StorageLifecycleConfig.description:

read-only and stay operator/vendor managed.  The backend only enforces phases
that are safe for the selected state store.  Today that means Elasticsearch ILM

The archive boundary is derived as ``hot_days + warm_days`` so independently
entered dates cannot drift.  Glacier is a desired archive target, not a claim
that the active state backend can restore directly from it.  This policy never
deletes active data.

ThresholdTuningConfig.description:
Nightly threshold auto-TUNING policy (Round 4). When enabled it observes per-rule FP rates and
PROPOSES bounded threshold adjustments (never applies them silently — the decision
stays deterministic, #3). ``min_samples`` is the minimum observations before a
suggestion is considered; ``max_n_step`` caps how far a correlation ``n`` may move
per cadence; ``fp_rate_target`` is the target false-positive rate; ``wilson_z`` is
the z-score for the Wilson confidence interval on the observed FP rate; ``ewma_alpha``
smooths the running FP-rate estimate; ``cadence`` is when the tuner runs; and
``shadow_eval`` (default ON) means a suggestion is EVALUATED against recent data
before it can be applied.

Observation defaults ON (Autopilot overhaul), while automatic writes default OFF.
The engine accepts only independent analyst outcomes, uses a Wilson lower bound plus
``min_samples``, proposes a bounded +1 (``max_n_step``) nudge, and runs mandatory
``shadow_eval`` before review or an explicitly enabled automatic application. A
suppression drop always routes to HITL. Rules with enough observed volume but too few
analyst labels produce an evidence-collection work item rather than silently training
on model output. Defaults follow ``STANDARDS.md``: ``min_samples=30`` (Wilson-stable;
hard floor 10), ``fp_rate_target=0.10`` (world-class SOC < 10% FP),
``wilson_z=1.96`` (0.95 confidence, lower bound), ``max_n_step=1`` (bounded nudge).
ThresholdTuningConfig.title: ThresholdTuningConfig

TimeRange.description:
The composer time window ``{from, to}`` (SPEC §3.1).

Each bound is ``now``, ``now-<n>[m|h|d|w|M|y]`` (lower-case ``m`` is minutes,
``M`` months, ``y`` years) or ISO-8601, and ``from`` may also be ``all``
(``{"from": "all"}``, the "All time" chip, Round 12, which never clamps); ``from``
must be strictly before ``to``, else 422. Round 12 (SPEC D7a): chat scope windows
have no span limit (:attr:`MAX_SPAN_DAYS` is ``None``). It applies to every
windowed chat tool; precedence is the model's explicit window from the user's
words, then this, then ``context.time_range``, then the tool's own default. Serialises as ``{"from",
"to"}`` (both keys, always) regardless of ``by_alias`` or ``exclude_defaults``, so
stored and wire shapes never diverge.
TimeRange.title: TimeRange

Every optional field here defaults to the WIDEST blast radius (enabled, unscoped,

silently re-enables a revoked declaration, clears its expiry, and widens it from one
source to all of them. So :func:`upsert_analyst_policy` carries prior values forward
for any field the client did not actually send (``model_fields_set``) — the same
reason :class:`_EnabledIn` makes ``enabled`` required.

operator has not saved yet). When ``policy`` is omitted the LIVE
``prefs.auto_close`` is used, so the caller sees exactly what the running system
would decide for these inputs. ``escalation_confidence`` / ``critical_severity``
default to the live prefs when omitted (they only affect the advisory ``escalate``
flag, never the close/route decision).

_PreviewIn.description:

(:class:`app.config.RuleMatch`); the preview reads recent events through the scoped

escalates, NEVER calls ``decide()``, NEVER bills the LLM (#6). The window + result
count are hard-capped exactly like ``GET /api/logs``.

get.description:
The session state the console boots from (PUBLIC).

Round 12: REGISTRY-AWARE. Beyond the JWT signature/``exp``/active-user check it
runs the same session-registry evaluation as every protected route (revocation,
per-user token version, idle and absolute limits — standard or remembered). When
the session has ended it answers ``authenticated: false`` with a ``reason``
(``revoked`` | ``idle_expired`` | ``absolute_expired`` | ``tv_mismatch``) and
clears the cookie, so the console lands on the sign-in page instead of a shell
where every call 401s. A session-store outage keeps trusting the JWT (as every
protected route does). A live session carries an additive ``session`` summary
``{remember, expires_at, idle_expires_at}``.

Round 14 (SPEC §4.4.5, D16): a signed-in answer also carries ``object_scoped``,
true when row-level (object) data scope applies to the viewer's case reads (the
rule the chat starters use, ``chat_starters.object_scoped``, failing closed), so
the Console hides case-derived dashboard panels instead of showing aggregates the
viewer could not read row by row. With sign-in off the answer is unchanged (no
viewer role, so no row scope: an absent ``object_scoped`` reads as false).

row goes to the Demo audit (SPEC §3.5).

get.description:
WHAT the precedent corpus is made of — now, and after a rebuild. Read-only.

**Reprojection is not the repair, and this endpoint is what proves it.** The
projection pages the case store newest-first, so on the deployment that motivated
this the bulk-confirmed cases were still the newest analyst-confirmed terminal cases:
a rebuild RE-SELECTS them and converges on the composition it just replaced. Worse,
the qualifying POOL was MORE skewed than the window drawn from it, so no selection
policy over that pool could have produced a healthy corpus. A successful rebuild is
therefore not evidence of repair, and "the job succeeded" must never be read as one.

What makes that visible, and what the payload carries:

* the JOINT (analyst outcome x model verdict) cross-tab, for the CURRENT corpus and
  for the projection a rebuild WOULD produce. Per-outcome counts alone read PRISTINE
  through the entire incident — a corpus that is 100% ``outcome=false_positive`` and
  also 100% ``verdict=NEEDS_HUMAN`` is telling the investigator "we escalated this
  every time", not "this is benign";
* per-rule counts, and chunk/document totals;
* the size of the qualifying POOL the bounded window was drawn from, so "200 of 889"
  is legible rather than implied;
* the admission CONCENTRATION — how much of the selected window one operator
  transaction bought.

It is deliberately a SEPARATE endpoint rather than a block inside
``/api/diagnostics/health``: deriving the would-be projection costs a bounded scan of
the case store, and the health rollup is polled by the Console. It costs **zero
embedding calls** either way — both halves come from a management read plus the
ordinary per-case projector, whose metadata already carries both axes.

Gated on ``settings:read`` like the rest of this router, seed-free, and advisory (#3).

get.description:
Browse recent logs across ALL enabled, browse-capable sources at once.

Fans out the EXACT per-source read that ``GET /sources/{id}/logs`` does — a bounded
scoped read-only search per PULL source (via ``es_client_for_source`` so per-source
TLS + mgmt-key-dropped, #1) and the live-tail buffer for each PUSH source — then
merges the rows newest-first. Every row carries a MANDATORY ``source_id`` +
``source_name`` provenance column. Read-only, hard-capped, and secrets are never
returned (rows are the same ``_log_row`` log-data shape).

Resilient by design: each source runs under ``asyncio.wait_for`` and the whole set
under ``gather(return_exceptions=True)``, so one slow or failing source degrades to
a per-source error entry and NEVER blocks the rest (partial success).

``source_id`` (OPTIONAL) scopes the fan-out to exactly one source, mirroring the
private preview reader in ``routes_rules._read_recent_events``. Omitting it is the
byte-identical all-sources behaviour. A ``source_id`` that is not visible in the
CURRENT mode is a 404 — while Demo Mode is active a real tenant id is
indistinguishable from an unknown one, so demo isolation leaks nothing — and a
visible id that is not an eligible browse target for this route (disabled, no
registered connector, or no ``browse`` capability) is a 501, the same status and
detail the per-source sibling route uses.

Each per-source status entry carries ``mode``: ``"search"`` = a real backing search
(``from``/``to``/``query`` apply) and ``"buffer"`` = a push source's process-local,
volatile in-memory live-tail ring, where ``from``/``to``/``query`` are IGNORED and
nothing survives a restart. Without it a caller cannot tell a time-ranged query from
a ring read in the merged view. ``mode`` describes the FILTERS, not the durability
of the backing store: a Demo Mode adapter reports ``"search"`` because it really
does apply ``from``/``to``/``query``.

BOUNDED, NOT COMPLETE. ``limit`` is clamped to 1..200 and applied per source AND on
the merge; there is NO pagination, cursor, or offset. The envelope echoes the
effective ``limit`` and a ``truncated`` flag so a caller can say "most recent N"
rather than implying it has seen everything. Each per-source status carries its own
``truncated``, computed by the SAME ``_browse_truncated`` rule the per-source
sibling route uses, and the envelope ``truncated`` is the OR of the merge being cut
with any single source being cut — so scoping to one source, or running a
single-source deployment, reports exactly what ``GET /sources/{id}/logs`` reports
for that same read.

Round 14 (SPEC §4.6.1) adds three EXACT filters, each bound as a structured filter
value and never as query text: ``rule`` (an equality match against any rule identity
of an event: its rule field, rule name field or classified suite rule; 1 to 256
characters on one line), ``severity`` (exactly one named level: ``info``, ``low``,
``medium``, ``high`` or ``critical``) and ``severity_gte`` (that level or above).
A level is projected through EACH source's own severity ceiling before it is
compared, so a 0 to 15 and a 0 to 100 source agree on what "High" means. Pull
sources compile the filters into their own query (exact); a push source's
live-tail ring is filtered here over the whole ring and, while a filter is active,
also kept to an explicit ``from``/``to`` (``now``, ``now-3d``, an ISO-8601 instant),
as a pull search and the rule summary are, so its rows and its "at least" total
describe the window the page names (``query`` still does not apply to a ring, and
``mode`` stays ``"buffer"``). While any of them is active the envelope echoes
``filters: {rule, severity, severity_gte}`` (``null`` = that one not filtered), so a
client can tell the filter was applied (an older backend ignores the parameters and
echoes nothing), and each per-source status carries ``exact``: ``false`` when that
source could only be filtered after a bounded read, so its rows are "at least"
these. A request with none of them is answered exactly as before, key for key. An
invalid value is a 400.

What this one does differently:

* anchors each case on its FIRST recorded ``{"event": "decision"}`` entry, so a

get.description:
Exact case or usage counts by one field (``by``) or two (``by`` then ``then``) over
a window, optionally bucketed by time (SPEC §4.4.2).

``kind=cases`` hands one ``CaseAggregateSpec`` (window, group_by, bucket, top_n,
filters; metrics ``count``, ``open_now`` and the two named families) to
``engine.case_aggregate.aggregate_cases``, the engine the chat's ``case_stats`` uses,
over the case store this caller reads (the Demo store while Demo Mode is on), with
the same prefs and operator timezone, so the dashboards and chat agree on every
number. The two families are never mixed: AI verdicts (``verdicted = verdict_tp +
verdict_fp + verdict_needs_human``) and the analyst outcome (``count = analyst_tp +
analyst_fp + analyst_ungraded``; analyst-policy closes are never graded). In an
un-bucketed row ``open_now`` is the window-exempt open stock: the open cases matching
the row whenever they were created, so it can exceed the row's windowed ``count``; in
a bucketed row it is the open part of that bucket's cohort. ``window_label`` is the
window as a caption start in sentence case ("Last 7 days (since 20 Oct 2026)"); a
relative window of days, weeks, months or years counts whole local periods exactly
as chat does, and an hours window (``now-168h``) is the rolling span the other
``window_hours`` metrics count, labelled as a board names it ("Last 7 days (since 21
Oct 2026, 12:00)"). ``multi_valued`` is true for ``rule``, ``mitre_tactic``
and ``mitre_technique``: a case counts once in each of its values, so rows never sum
to ``total``. ``exact`` false (``partial`` true, with ``partial_reason``) marks lower
bounds; a zero is never invented for a figure that was not measured. Cases with no
readable creation date are disclosed in ``missing_created`` (``missing_in_total``
says whether ``total`` holds them), and with buckets cut by ``top`` each bucket's
``other_count`` holds its share of ``other``.

``kind=usage`` aggregates the usage ledger (``engine.case_aggregate.aggregate_usage``,
metrics ``calls`` and ``cost_usd``, ranked by spend) and is gated on ``cost:view``.

One answer per question is shared for a few seconds and a question being read is
joined, never read twice; at most two reads run at once, a read gets a bounded time,
an answer holds at most 5,000 group rows and the shared answers 20,000 in all. Every read
folds the cases of the window, because the analyst outcome family needs the case
model; the fold reads only the stored fields its metrics and groups need.

Errors: ``400 breakdown_bad_param`` (an unknown value, ``then`` equal to ``by``, a
case-only parameter with ``kind=usage``, an empty ``filter_rule``, a ``top`` that is
not a whole number from 1 to 50, a window it cannot read, too many buckets, or
``top`` times the buckets over 5,000 rows); ``403`` without the grant; ``409
breakdown_scope_unsupported`` for a case breakdown while row-level data scope applies
to the caller (aggregates do not honour row scope yet, SPEC D16); ``503
breakdown_unavailable`` when the store could not be read at all or the read ran past
its time (nothing was measured, so no figure is returned). A read: no audit row, no
model call (#6), aggregates only (#7); nothing here is read by
``case_manager.decide()`` (#3).

``_STORE_FETCH_LIMIT`` or the read failed partway — the outcome tallies are then a
lower bound and ``store_total``/``fetched`` say by how much). When the counters are still warming

headline ``reduction.overall_pct`` is a DASH, so the UI degrades to a case-only funnel.

``events_per_min`` (Round 14, SPEC §4.4.3, the detection board's "Events per minute")
is the mean raw alerts per minute over the whole hours the counters summed
(:func:`_events_per_min`), rounded to 0.01. When the counters began inside the
window (``counters.incomplete``, a fresh install, a Demo) the hour they began in is
left out, because it can hold a backfilled burst (a cold-start lookback, the Demo's
history written at once): the rate then covers the hours after it. ``null`` while
``counters.available`` is false or less than five minutes are measured, never a
made-up 0 and never a burst read as a rate. ``events_per_min_since`` is the ISO
start of the span the rate covers (``null`` with no rate) and
``events_per_min_reason`` a plain sentence saying why the rate is not measured or,
when the counters began inside the window, that it covers only the time since the
end of the hour they began in (``null`` when the rate covers the whole window).

every case the window (and, for ``compare=prev``, the preceding window) reaches
(Round 12). ``truncated`` is True when that span holds more cases than
``_STORE_FETCH_LIMIT`` or the read failed partway; ``store_total`` is then the exact
number of in-scope cases and ``fetched`` the newest analysed, and
``window_covered`` says whether the SELECTED window is still complete.

equal-length window. SLA targets come from ``Preferences.sla`` (advisory; #3).

The headline populations, and which of them ``window_hours`` bounds — the five
Console tiles are built on exactly these and they are NOT interchangeable::

    {"case_count": int,                     # arrival cohort in-window, policy-closed INCLUDED
     "severity_counts": {"critical": int, "high": int, "medium": int,
                         "low": int, "info": int},   # partitions case_count exactly
     "open_now": {"count": int, "window_exempt": true, "as_of": iso8601,
                  "complete": bool, "reason": str},  # STOCK, measured now, NOT windowed
     "quality": {"terminal_cases": int, "auto_closed_cases": int,
                 "human_closed_cases": int, "system_closed_cases": int,
                 "false_positive_rate": float, ...},
     "truncated": bool, "store_total": int, "fetched": int,
     "window_covered": bool, "window_coverage_reason": str,
     "oldest_fetched_at": iso8601 | null}

* ``severity_counts`` is server-side and covers the FULL windowed population; it
  exists so no client has to infer a band total from whatever bounded page of
  cases it happens to hold. Bands are the read-time advisory ladder
  (``engine.priority.band_of_case``), resolved against each source's DECLARED
  severity ceiling — hence ``Preferences`` is threaded in. Nothing is persisted.
* ``open_now`` is deliberately window-EXEMPT and carries ``window_exempt: true``
  so it can never be rendered as summing with the windowed tiles.
  ``aging.queue_depth`` is the cohort-scoped "arrived in-window and still open"
  number and is a different figure.
* ``auto_closed_cases`` + ``human_closed_cases`` + ``system_closed_cases`` sum
  EXACTLY to ``terminal_cases``. Render all three or none: the residual (SYSTEM
  routing + legacy records with no recorded decider) must stay visible even at 0,
  and human work is NEVER ``terminal_cases - auto_closed_cases``. These report the
  LAST recorded decider — see ``engine.metrics.quality_metrics`` for the caveat a
  "human vs AI" surface must disclose.
* ``window_covered`` is the honest-coverage flag: whether the SELECTED window is
  fully answerable from the cases that were read (cutoff at or after
  ``oldest_fetched_at``). With the exact population it is True unless a single
  window outgrew the in-memory bound. ``open_now`` is an exact store COUNT (window
  exempt) and carries its own ``complete`` flag.
* A case-store OUTAGE soft-fails to an empty fetch so the dashboard never 500s.
  Both completeness flags then go False with a reason naming the failure: the
  counts are still zeros, but zero-because-unreadable is not a measurement and must
  never be published as one. ``truncated`` is unchanged (it compares fetched with
  store-reported total, and both are 0).

is live until it is explicitly approved.

(the deployment whose approvals were broken for its whole life) otherwise grows
without bound and keeps rendering month-old recommendations as actionable. The
sweep is bounded, writes nothing when nothing has lapsed, and is best-effort: the
store's read-time projection already presents a lapsed row as ``expired``, so a
failed sweep costs durability, never honesty.

post.description:
Reject many proposals in one audited request.

A queue that accumulated for a deployment's whole life cannot realistically be
cleared one HTTP request at a time, but convenience must not buy itself a hole in
the append-only audit trail (#2). This therefore runs the SAME strict per-proposal
decision path as :func:`reject_proposal` — one ``event_id``-keyed append-only
decision record each — rather than a bulk state write with a single summary row.

Consequences of that choice, all deliberate:

* **Idempotent.** An already-rejected id reports ``already_rejected`` and writes
  nothing new; ``record_strict`` deduplicates on ``event_id`` anyway.
* **Partial success is a first-class result.** One unusable id — missing, in
  flight, or a store hiccup — is reported in ``results`` and never aborts the
  batch, so an operator is never left guessing which half landed.
* **Bounded.** At most :data:`BULK_DECISION_LIMIT` ids per request, deduplicated,
  because each one performs a durable write.

Expired proposals are rejectable, which is what makes this the queue-clearing tool.

schema.title: Response Bulk Reject Proposals Api Proposals Bulk Reject Post

post.description:
Approve or acknowledge a pending proposal through its kind-specific path.

suppression → materialise a ``SuppressionRule`` from the payload and append it to
``Preferences.suppression_rules`` via the settings write path so the cost gate
picks it up LIVE. memory → append a human-injectable agent fact. tuning →
revalidate and, where eligible, materialise the bounded change. ``automation_ack``
records review only and never mutates configuration, Memory, suppression, or case
state.

The decision runs in four ordered phases — PREPARE (pure validation only),
AUDIT (the strict ``event_id``-keyed decision record), EFFECT, FINALISE — so an
operator who is told the approval failed can never find the configuration already
changed by that attempt. Every phase is idempotent: the strict claim fixes actor
and audit timestamp, ``record_strict`` deduplicates on ``event_id``, and every
effect is keyed by proposal id, so a retry after any failure converges on exactly
one applied change. 404 if missing; 409 if already decided/in progress, if the
proposal has EXPIRED, or if its evidence basis can no longer be verified — the
last two are refusals to act on stale reasoning and ask for a re-draft, and both
happen before anything is audited or applied.

post.description:

Rejection has no effect phase at all: preferences, Memory, suppression and case
state are never touched, so the ordering is simply strict CAS claim → strict
append-only decision record → strict finalisation. An EXPIRED proposal may still
be rejected — retiring dead review work is how a queue is cleared and it changes
nothing. 404 if missing; 409 if already decided/in progress.
